play.comment: Pelle Larsson's cutting dunk off Davion Mitchell's pass with 7 seconds left that made it 108–105, out of a Heat timeout. An original illustration from the play-by-play and written accounts; not traced from footage, not to scale.
play.head: Larsson cuts for the dunk
play.subL: Pelle Larsson cuts to the rim, 7 seconds left, up 106–105

aria: Animated recap of the Heat's 108 to 105 win at New York: Pelle Larsson's cutting dunk with 7 seconds left that made it 108 to 105, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Giannis Antetokounmpo's 22 points and career-high 23 rebounds, the top scorers, how the Heat won, and the next game.

figure.label: Pelle Larsson, listed 6-5, 215 lb, No. 9 (Wikipedia); no sourced wingspan

notes: Box score from the Covers matchup page for the Heat's 108–105 win at Madison Square Garden on Nov 27, 2026, an NBA Cup group game: all 108 Miami points and all 105 New York points add up from the player lines, as do the field goals and threes. Team totals (39 of 90, 11 of 45 from three, 19 of 27 FT for Miami; 37 of 79, 8 of 32, 23 of 30 for New York), rebounds (43–42), points in the paint (46–42), fast-break points (10–17) and points off turnovers (20–13) are on Fox Sports' box score; assists (26–29) and steals (13–7) on CBS Sports' gametracker and the Covers player totals. The quarter scores (31–29–26–22 to 21–23–35–26) are on Covers and CBS; 60–44 at the half and 86–79 after three are also in the Sun-Sentinel and Field Level Media. The biggest leads (Miami 23, New York 1) are on Covers; the NY Daily News has the 23 at 54–31 with 3:47 left in the second quarter. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Friday's games.

Giannis Antetokounmpo had 22 points and a career-high 23 rebounds (AP) and passed 22,000 career points (Sun-Sentinel). Bam Adebayo led Miami with 25. The Knicks came all the way back and took their first lead, 92–91, on Pacome Dadiet's reverse layup with 6:23 left (Field Level Media). With 9 seconds left Jalen Brunson was fouled on a three and made two of three free throws to cut it to 106–105 (CBS play-by-play; Sun-Sentinel; NY Daily News). The win ended the Knicks' six-game winning streak and their NBA Cup title defense (AP; NY Daily News). Miami finished 3–1 in group play but lost the group tiebreaker to Philadelphia (Yahoo Sports). Miami has won 11 of 14 since an 0–4 start (Field Level Media). OG Anunoby, Andre Drummond, Miles McBride and Jordan Clarkson were out for New York (NY Daily News; Field Level Media). Next: Miami plays at Cleveland on Sunday (Sun-Sentinel); New York hosts Atlanta on Sunday (NY Daily News).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Pelle Larsson's dunk with 7 seconds left that made it 108–105: CBS Sports' play-by-play has "Pelle Larsson makes two point cutting dunk (Davion Mitchell assists)" at 0:07 for 106–105 to 108–105, right after a Heat timeout at 0:09; Field Level Media: "Larsson inbounded the ball to Mitchell and then darted around Josh Hart ... before taking a feed from Mitchell and dunking"; the NY Daily News and NY Post give 7.2 seconds. So the board's Heat +1 to +3 is 106–105 to 108–105. Brunson then missed a pull-up three at the buzzer (CBS). The inbound and the pass are not drawn: the play is shown as the template's plain finish at the rim. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Miami Heat or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Larsson's listed 6-foot-5 and 215 pounds (Wikipedia); no wingspan was found in the sources read, so his arms are drawn at his height. He wears the Heat's road red with No. 9 (Wikipedia) and a proposed look from kit/looks.json. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
